target: Tc, 2D square-lattice Ising model (J=1, k_B=1, h=0)
method: Binder-cumulant crossing between L=16 and L=32 (cubic fit of U4_16 - U4_32 over a 7-point T window, single root taken as Tc)
notes: Fix stage applied ising.py changes 1-6 from referee.md (sigma(Tc) via 2000-draw noise Monte Carlo, run-time tolerance = 3 sigma + 0.002 finite-size bound, corrected docstring bound, sys.exit(1) instead of bare assert, corrected notes sentence, and the standard MEASURED/PUBLISHED/ERROR_ESTIMATE/TOLERANCE/ABS_DIFF/RUNTIME_S/RESULT print block). Two full verify2 runs gave identical numeric lines (MEASURED=2.2675, ERROR_ESTIMATE=0.0025, TOLERANCE=0.0094, ABS_DIFF=0.0017, RESULT=PASS in both), so the result is deterministic under the fixed seed (SEED=20260922); only wall-clock runtime differed (135.2 s vs 178.8 s), both well inside the 240 s per-run timeout. Recomputed abs_diff = |2.2675 - 2.269185| = 0.001685, matching the printed ABS_DIFF=0.0017 within the script's 4-decimal rounding. Pass holds on 3 sigma alone (3 sigma = 0.0074 > abs_diff 0.0017); tolerance is now measured (3 x sigma(Tc) + 0.002 finite-size bound) rather than the old fixed TOL=0.05 (a 20-sigma band). U4 at the crossing came out to 0.6124, close to the ~0.61 expected for the square lattice with periodic boundaries, so the crossing is not a fluke. No warnings or errors on stderr in either run. Referee change 5 applied: this notes field no longer claims bit-identical repeats are a precision check, and no longer says the docstring's asserted 0.005 bias is 'smaller than' the observed 0.0017 deviation -- per referee change 3, the run's own U16(Tc) vs U*=0.61069 bound now bounds the shift below about 0.0016, and the sign is not resolved. Previous (pre-fix, verify1) values for comparison: measured=2.267460, tolerance=0.05, abs_diff=0.001725314, pass=true, runtime_s=85.2, error_estimate not printed (script previously printed no ERROR_ESTIMATE/TOLERANCE/ABS_DIFF/RESULT block; results/ising.json was filled from free-text lines).
